transcript:
Header: Recorded 2026-03-15 14:00 PDT; Duration 54 minutes; Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Lisa Chen (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (CTO - Evergreen Tech), Priya Singh (Security Lead), Jordan Lee (IT Ops), Alicia Gomez (Legal)

Summary: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review. Customer wants access to reports, controls mapping to their reqs, trust center access; questions about encryption (KMS), RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency, and private deployment options.

[00:00] Sam Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Sam from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, joined by lisa our solutions eng; quick roll call?
[00:07] Mark Rivera: mark here, priya, jordan, alicia on our side, thanks for taking the time.
[00:12] Lisa Chen: hi all, lisa here, i'll be the SE on the call. we'll walk through SOC 2 artifacts, trust center access and controls mapping.
[00:20] Priya Singh: great, high level our procurement asked for SOC 2 type II reports, ISO 27001 attestation if available, plus details on encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integrations, and RBAC with SSO.
[00:32] Sam Patel: perfect. quick note on scope: Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments; most of the security artifacts live in our trust center and we can provide controls mapping that ties Redwood controls to ISO 27001 clauses and the AICPA Trust Services Criteria.
[00:45] Jordan Lee: when you say trust center, is that a link we can share with procurement or do we need NDAs?
[00:52] Sam Patel: trust center link is shareable; for full reports (SOC 2 Type II PDF) we usually require a signed NDA or an access request we can send the standard access form. we'll include a read-only link for the control matrix.
[01:05] Alicia Gomez: legal will want to review the SOC report and the encryption key ownership language, specifically whether customer keys are supported.
[01:12] Lisa Chen: absolutely. quick clarification: hosted API uses Redwood-managed keys by default; we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted, we also offer bring-your-own-key for higher tiers i'll detail that in the notes.
[01:30] Mark Rivera: how does that work for multi-tenant hosted environments? do keys isolate per-customer?
[01:36] Lisa Chen: in hosted, Redwood manages the master keys and uses per-tenant envelope keys, but master key is Redwood-managed unless you enable BYOK; for Dedicated and Private you can attach your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault or HSM). there's an extra controls checklist for BYOK.
[01:52] Priya Singh: we need confirmation that KMS integration provides key separation and that logs show key usage. auditability is critical.
[01:59] Lisa Chen: yes, KMS logs are surfaced in the audit logs; we can show an example event set i'll attach sample logs (sanitized) and the mapping to the Redwood audit schema.
[02:12] Sam Patel: another common ask: RBAC and SSO. we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with predefined roles plus custom role support for enterprise tenants.
[02:23] Jordan Lee: do roles map to specific API scopes (like read-only tokens for embeddings)? do you have token-level scoping?
[02:29] Lisa Chen: good q. we have per-route and per-token ACLs roles can be bound to policies that restrict model access, route access and usage quotas. token-level scoping exists for service tokens. there may be some differences for dedicated vs hosted in the console UX but capabilities are the same.
[02:47] Mark Rivera: how far back do audit logs go and can we export to our SIEM?
[02:52] Lisa Chen: by default hosted includes 90 days; enterprise retention can be customized (longer retention on Dedicated/Private). logs can be exported via S3 sink or streamed to SIEM via Kafka/Logstash connectors.
[03:05] Priya Singh: is the audit log schema documented? we need field-level names for mapping and the retention policy for exports.
[03:12] Lisa Chen: yes, we'll share the audit schema doc; the mapping spreadsheet will include field names, event types, and retention details.
[03:20] Sam Patel: let's talk controls mapping we typically map Redwood controls to SOC 2 CC and ISO 27001 Annex A. some examples: encryption at rest -> A.10/A.18, access control -> A.9, vendor management -> A.15. we'll send a full matrix.
[03:35] Mark Rivera: do you have independent ISO 27001 certs? we've seen a mix of vendors who are SOC 2 and others who are ISO.
[03:41] Sam Patel: Redwood currently holds SOC 2 Type II covering the hosted control set; we're in progress on ISO 27001 certification for the control plane and expect timeline Q3 2026 i'll include the roadmap. for Dedicated/Private customers, we can provide environment-specific attestations as part of contractual commitments.
[03:58] Alicia Gomez: for procurement we need to know which controls are in scope for hosted vs dedicated; the control matrix needs that callout.
[04:05] Lisa Chen: noted, the spreadsheet will have a column for deployment scope (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) for each control.
[04:12] Priya Singh: on data residency, we need guaranteed region selection and assurance that tokens and payloads won't be replicated outside region.
[04:20] Lisa Chen: we support regional routing and pinned deployments for dedicated and private; hosted has region selection but some global services (control plane metadata) may be in other regions details in the data residency DOC. we'll highlight what data is kept local vs global (logging metadata vs user content).
[04:35] Jordan Lee: curious about KV cache and caching of prompts; do you persist prompts and if so how long? customers want to opt-out of retention.
[04:43] Lisa Chen: by default we keep short-term KV caches for performance but we do allow no-retention or customer-controlled retention policies; also there is an option to disable prefix caching in Dedicated/Private.
[04:55] Mark Rivera: rough question on latency vs cost: if we go Dedicated with BYOK and longer retention, is cost significantly higher?
[05:02] Sam Patel: Dedicated adds base capacity costs; BYOK has a small per-month admin surcharge depending on HSM usage. we'll surface a cost delta in the quote; lisa can run a cost/perf estimate for your workload pattern.
[05:15] Lisa Chen: i'll need sample traffic patterns. we can model token throughput, typical sequence lengths and provide batching/quantization recommendations to hit cost targets.
[05:25] Priya Singh: from security perspective, what's the breach notification SLA and incident handling process?
[05:31] Sam Patel: included in standard enterprise contract: 24-48 hour initial notification windows for high severity incidents, forensic support and SOC access. we'll share the incident response playbook redacted.
[05:45] Alicia Gomez: also want to confirm subprocessor list and subprocessors' SOC/ISO posture.
[05:50] Lisa Chen: subprocessor list is in trust center; we note each subprocessor's attestation where available.
[06:00] Mark Rivera: ok good. procurement will ask for references and evidence for continuity planning. do you have BCP / DR docs?
[06:06] Sam Patel: yes, those are in the trust center; we have RTO/RPO targets for dedicated clusters documented per region.
[06:14] Priya Singh: one more technical item: KMS key rotation and zero-knowledge claims if we manage the keys, can you guarantee no plaintext access?
[06:22] Lisa Chen: our runtime never stores plaintext keys; the models run on memory and we have hardware protections; with BYOK/HSM you retain control of key lifecycle. we'll include the cryptographic controls summary.
[06:36] Speaker 1: [inaudible]... does the model caching store derivatives of user content?
[06:41] Lisa Chen: caching is limited to inference acceleration (KV caches) and not used for training; we do not use customer content for model training unless explicitly opted in.
[06:50] Mark Rivera: great. next steps and wrap up?
[06:54] Sam Patel: recap: we'll share SOC 2 report (NDA), trust center link, controls mapping, audit log schema, KMS integration doc and sample logs; lisa will run controls mapping and cost estimate. schedule follow up: KMS/SE deep dive next week.
[07:08] Priya Singh: thanks, please include legal contact for contract language around BYOK/HSM and data residency.
[07:14] Sam Patel: noted, alicia i'll send the contract contact and standard clauses.
[07:19] Jordan Lee: i'll set up an internal folder for evidence collection and invite sam.
[07:24] Sam Patel: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendared deep-dive.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-attributions and ASR artifacts. Shared artifacts referenced: Trust Center link (to be sent), SOC 2 Type II PDF (NDA), Controls mapping spreadsheet (Redwood -> ISO/SOC), sample audit logs (sanitized), KMS integration guide.

End of call.
